prompt: Adding the total column to the index made the query an index-only scan.
why: When the index holds every column needed, the table isn't read. That's a covering index.
trap: The plan reports it, but the change was covering.

prompt: The index uses INCLUDE (name, price) so the listing never touches the table.
why: INCLUDE columns make the index cover the query without changing its order.
trap: It's not denormalising the table; it's the index.

prompt: The query uses an index for filtering but still reads the table because of SELECT *.
why: Selecting only needed columns lets an index cover the query.
trap: The index works; the star stops it covering.

prompt: Counting orders per user reads only the (user_id) index, never the order rows.
why: The index alone answers the query. It covers it.
trap: It's not a precomputed count; it's the index.

prompt: The plan shows an index scan with millions of heap fetches for columns not in the index.
why: Each row needs a table lookup. Covering the needed columns removes them.
trap: An index is used; it doesn't cover.

prompt: The team stopped adding columns to the index when it grew larger than the table.
why: Covering has a cost: bigger indexes and slower writes.
trap: It's the trade-off of covering, not order.
